title: The 2026 Denverite gift guide
summary: We chose some our favorite stuff that can become your favorite stuff.
content: Thanksgiving has come and gone, which means the season of gift-giving (and shopping) has fully arrived. If you love shopping small, trawling through a holiday market and discovering a new favorite place or artisan on your gift-buying journey, this is the guide for you. We each chose a few of our favorite items, services and stores to share with you. Paolo’s picks Enjoy Colfax One of my most complimented sweaters is from Lawrence and Larimer, the vibe-y apparel store on Colfax Avenue. Featuring a new cream base and an illustration that reads “Colfax Athletic Club”, I get one of two comments when I wear it to the office: “Oooh, where’d you get that?” or “Is that a real running club?” The sweatshirt is no longer available, but the design is currently on a T-shirt . All Colfax tee’s cost $40. If your heart is set on a crew, Lawrence and Larimer currently has some available with their boxing bee logo for $70. Grab a piece of history Readers, be warned: I am not the biggest fan of the Denver Summit FC’s inaugural kits. They’re a little plain, lacking the patterns or designs that make a soccer kit truly iconic. (My favorite recent kit, for example, is this stunning bright yellow and navy blue kit from Tottenham Hotspur.) But those Summit kits will have something irreplicable: history. Clubs only have their first kit once, and with the Summit’s inaugural season over, these ones won’t be around for much longer . A blank authentic kit costs $122.50, a blank replica kit will run you $77 and a replica kit with Lindsey Heaps’ name and number comes in at $105. All are currently $30 off. Consider picking up one for the biggest soccer fan in your life. Buy your pal the best gym deal west of the Mississippi There are just a few days left to take advantage of the city’s November membership sale for rec centers. For just $258, you get access to all of the city’s recreation centers for a year. That means you’ll have unlimited access to the gyms, pools, basketball courts and more offered across the city. (It even includes the outdoor pools!) Memberships are cheaper for people ages 2-24 and over 65, or if you opt for a local or neighborhood membership, which limits access to smaller rec centers. Adding someone else from your household also costs just half the price of the base membership. Alex’s picks Build the perfect gift package on your coffee run Weathervane Cafe is an excellent coffee shop, perfect for meeting a friend or curling up with a book. But it’s also one of the best places to find trinkets to round out some stockings or a gift bundle. On a recent trip, here were some of my favorites: An ornament of a felted rabbit holding some holly ($10) A pocket kite, for when the whimsy and the wind move you ($18) A mug emblazoned with “Not today, Blucifer” and the horse himself ($26) A zine about the history of gay pirate tattoos ($5) A hand-poured candle in an old Coors Banquet can ($18) And after you finish your shopping, you get to treat yourself to a sandwich and coffee of your choice. (I would do the curry chicken salad sandwich and iced latte, myself.) Help your giftee’s skin survive winter Denver is always dry. This time of year, it’s also cold. Treat your loved one with a gift card to Jalan Facial Spa . The Uptown spa is luxurious and well worth the investment, especially if they come in with a gift card to cover or knock down the price. Through Dec. 23, the spa is also offering discounts on certain increments of gift cards (e.g. buy $115, get $15 off). Perfect for the luxurious procrastinator. Gift a bit of luck Loved one having a rough year? Gift them some good vibes for 2027 with a beautiful horseshoe from Palomino Home. The shoes are wrapped in colorful fibers and have a leather strap to hang wherever the heart desires. Buy a ready-made one , or make a custom order (both $45). Their online store also has a number of adorable prints and accessories, including a one-of-a-kind “silly filly” painting ($25) that is calling my name. Catch Palamino Home in person at Rainbow Dome’s Holigay Market on Saturday, Dec. 12. Charm your loved one The Story We Wear is a new store from Sarah O., aka the jeweler that seemingly sells most Denverites their engagement and wedding bands (me and my wife included). (Ed. note: Us too. -AK) The new shop specializes in vintage jewelry and other estate-sale finds, plus charms and engraving. Most of the shopping has to be done in person, but a few charms are available online in a holiday pop-up . While some of the charms climb into the hundreds or even above $1,000, there are some deals: A tiny skier ($90)! A petite house ($90)! While you’re there, consider a practical jewelry lover’s gift, like a cleaning kit ($40) or cute travel case ($49). Kiara’s picks Give the gift of smelling good Ode To Perfume is a fragrance boutique on South Pearl that offers in-person sessions to help people find their signature scent. The shop also has goods like candles, lotions and incense. Book someone a free 45-minute fragrance consultation with one of their professionals and get them started with some sample perfumes you think they would enjoy. Discovery sets start at $25 and go up to $151. Take a tea tour This destination is a little outside of Denver but well worth the drive. Give the gift of really yummy tea at Celestial Seasonings in Boulder. You could, of course, buy them a bunch of tea. Most standard boxes of tea will run you about $5.50 , while gift boxes cost between $36-$60 . Or, take it to the next level and go on a tour with them. For $6 a person , you can tour the factory and see where the magic happens. Tours last about 45 minutes and run from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m., Tuesday to Saturday. Support the library and buy your loved ones books The Red Chair Bookshop out of the Denver Central Library is a great — and affordable — place to buy used books while supporting the library. They have an online store (right now you could grab Courtney Barnett’s “MTV Unplugged Live In Melbourne” for $10 , a J.R.R. Tolkien art book for $26.75 and hundreds of other items). You can also visit the storefront off the Broadway side of the library’s first floor. The magic of movies Do you have a certified cinephile in your life? Give the gift of great movies with a Denver Film membership : $65 for one person and $125 for a duo. Members get discounts on tickets and concessions at the Sie Film Center — including an all-day happy hour — plus free member-only screenings and early access to tickets for the Denver Film Festival. Camelia’s picks Browse this design studio-bookstore Looking for stationery, books or art prints? The Shop at Matter truly has it all. I am a bookstore fanatic and was in awe of their book selection, including authors of color and rare finds. (Who knew James Baldwin wrote a poetry collection? It’s called “Jimmy’s Blues,” and you can buy it for $17.) Plus, this store functions as a design studio with printing press events and drawers filled with art made in-house . You can also buy items like a 500-piece puzzle with art by Colorado’s own Caroline Clark ($36), an adorable kids flatware set ($34-$38) and stickers of Black literature icons ($4.50) . And, of course, you could always just get a gift card . If you’re looking to impress your super artsy friend, this is the place to shop! Go nuts for some cinnamon roasted nuts You may be thinking nuts are a weird gift … but haven’t we all found ourselves looking for an easy but luxurious gift that isn’t as basic as a box of chocolates? May I introduce you to Bob’s Roasted Nuts . (Sorry to all my nut allergists!) I found Bob’s during my first visit to the ChristKindlmarket at the Auraria campus. Don’t let the crowds of people and the beautiful lights distract you from the wafting smells of spiced cinnamon and freshly roasted and toasted nuts. This is the real deal. A small is $9 and comes wrapped in a red-and-white checkered paper cone. These nuts are so beautiful and warm that I wish I had bought a large one. If you can’t make it to the market itself, lucky for you (and me), Bob’s Roasted Nuts delivers. Buy an at-home cone for $9, a family-size bag for $16, a party-size bag for $25 or even a custom tray of nuts for $50. We won’t tell anyone if it’s for a party of one. Andy’s pick The ski train I have taken the Winter Park Express exactly once, when it first returned to service a decade ago. It was some real Polar Express stuff. (By which I mean a magical train ride through a snowy wonderland, not a dive into the uncanny valley with CGI Tom Hanks. ) A decade on, the rebooted service has not only expanded — it’s gotten cheaper. You can snag tickets for as little as $18 roundtrip for a weekday. Weekends run $38. And there are discounts for kids 12 and under, seniors, military members and people with disabilities. The train departs Union Station at 7 a.m. on Thursdays through Sundays, from Dec. 10 to April 4. It leaves the resort at 4:35 p.m. Expect a two-hour trip. Theoretically, you’ll get there faster on a good driving day, but the train is also less stressful, more fun, safer and less prone to apocalyptic traffic scenarios. The train lets off just a short walk from the lifts and main lodge on the Winter Park side of the resort. My recommendation: Commit now to a date in February or early March, so you and your giftee(s) can get the best conditions while skipping winter driving. To book tickets, head to Amtrak and enter “DEN” as the departing station and “WPR” as the return station. Be sure to book the Winter Park Express, not the Zephyr, which will land you in a shuttle-served lot instead of the resort platform. And if you’re not ready to commit to a date, buy your boo an Amtrak gift card!
